question.prompt: Ricardo has \(2020\) coins, some of which are pennies (\(1\)-cent coins) and the rest of which are nickels (\(5\)-cent coins). He has at least one penny and at least one nickel. What is the difference in cents between the greatest possible and least possible amounts of money that Ricardo can have?

solutions.explanation:
Set aside one penny and one nickel, since Ricardo must have at least one of each. The remaining \(2020-2=2018\) coins determine the difference between the greatest and least possible amounts.

For the greatest amount, make all those remaining coins nickels. For the least, make all of them pennies. Changing each penny to a nickel adds \(5-1=4\) cents, so the difference is

\[
2018\cdot4=\boxed{8072}\text{ cents},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). The two set-aside coins contribute equally in both cases and cancel from the comparison.
solutions.title: Hold one coin of each type fixed and compare the remaining coins
